# ONLY 3 LEFT

> An educational field guide to dark patterns and deceptive UX. 46 named patterns across 10 categories, each with a definition, real examples, the psychological mechanism, the legal context and an ethical alternative. Available in English and Spanish.

Canonical site: https://only3left.vercel.app
Primary language: English (en). Alternate: Spanish (es), under /es.
Licence for the dataset: CC BY 4.0, attribution required.

## Start here

- [What are dark patterns? Definition, types and examples](https://only3left.vercel.app/dark-patterns): the pillar page.
- [Full catalogue](https://only3left.vercel.app/patterns): all 46 patterns with severity ratings.
- [Categories](https://only3left.vercel.app/categories): the ten-family taxonomy.

## Key pattern pages

- [Roach Motel](https://only3left.vercel.app/patterns/roach-motel): easy to enter, hard to leave.
- [Fake Scarcity](https://only3left.vercel.app/patterns/fake-scarcity): invented stock and demand.
- [Confirmshaming](https://only3left.vercel.app/patterns/confirmshaming): refusal copy that insults.
- [Misdirection](https://only3left.vercel.app/patterns/misdirection): attention routed away from cost.
- [Paywall Tease](https://only3left.vercel.app/patterns/paywall-tease): commitment before the wall.

## Machine-readable

- [Dataset (JSON)](https://only3left.vercel.app/dataset.json): every pattern with slug, category, severity, psychology, examples and the ethical alternative. CC BY 4.0.
- [Sitemap](https://only3left.vercel.app/sitemap.xml): both locales with hreflang alternates.

## Sources

The catalogue cites Harry Brignull's deceptive.design, Mathur et al. (2019) "Dark Patterns at Scale", the FTC's 2022 dark patterns report, and the EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive.
